To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
7-[2-(4-piperidinyl)ethyl]hexahydroazepine-2-one (7-PPEA) is a novel, potent and highly selective adenosine A2a receptor antagonist.
theophylline derivatives, in which the terminal lactam is hexahydroazapin-2-one or 2,3,4,4a,5,9a-hexahydro-1H-pyrido[1,2-b]azepin-6-one, have the potential to become cognitive enhancers.
theophylline and its analogs have potential as nootropic agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and structure-activity relationships of theophyllines.
the synthesis and neuroactivity of a series of theophyllines and their analogs.
the design and synthesis of new theophylline derivatives with improved neuroactivity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
theophylline derivatives with the lactam ring are promising nootropic drugs.
these theophylline derivatives may have potential for further study as nootropic agents.
theophylline and its analogs may be nootropics or cognitive enhancers, and the mechanism of action is probably related to adenosine receptor antagonism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the length of carbon chain on N1 and the size of the terminal hetero ring strongly influence the activity of theophyllines.
theophylline and its analogs are not only bronchodilators and anti-inflammatory agents but also have potential as cognitive enhancers.
theophylline derivatives are promising candidates for further studies of nootropic activity in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
theophylline derivatives can be used to modulate the activity of the hippocampus and may therefore have potential for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases.

theophylline is a promising scaffold for the development of new nootropic drugs.
